C-PAYMENT-RECORD.Summary: Make already-discharged findings retirable by recording their payments as historical registry rows the derivation can read. PaidBy is derived, not authored; a payment nobody recorded is a payment that never happened, as far as the ratchet is concerned. Archived specs are never edited. kind="historical" is a new closed-union member, and the payer-row filter is widened to see it — reusing kind="chartered" would be a lie, and a new kind that the filter does not admit is inert. Four historical rows land in live registry.xml naming archived bundles, then --retire moves the rows and the paid findings in one invocation before any committed tree can breach the registry ceiling. Pays F90, F90.1, F35, F27, F27.1, F27.2, F38, each verified against the present tree, not against a finding's own discharge sentence. Binding live rulings D28, D28.1, D30, D11; staged D36 charters this name at position 6. This bundle's purpose is to write the record; D30 is scoped, not skirted. Name accepted: no archive directory, no live or retired registry row, staged charter only.
C-PAYMENT-RECORD.Problem:
A finding retires when its PaidBy child names an archived bundle, and PaidBy is derived from registry rows (and a phrase in archived specs). Seventy-one archived bundles exist; eleven are named by any registry row (all eleven are retired chartered rows). Sixty archived bundles are invisible to the derivation. Zero live findings are currently eligible (validate-record-retirement.ts exits 0), so --retire moves nothing, the findings window stays at H = 252, and the staged buffer cannot be flushed. Staged F187 named this; the circularity is F183's: the findings that would fuel the window are themselves in the buffer.
The present-tree witnesses for already- discharged findings are not in the payer map, because those bundles have no registry row and their specs never use the payer phrase (/\bthe paid findings?\b/i at scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:40, :483). Measured: C-CURSOR-TASK-RESOLVER, C-SUBSTANCE-OVER-NAME, C-DECLARED-WRITES, and C-GRAMMAR-SEAM are all archived applied, all absent from both registry files, all lacking the phrase.
kind is a closed TypeScript union ("chartered" | "sweep-remainder") at scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:69. charteredRowsFromRoot (:729-737) keeps only (row.attributes.kind ?? "chartered") === "chartered". A new kind is invisible unless both sites widen. Reusing chartered is semantically false: these bundles were never chartered in this registry.
D30 freezes the record for a bundle that measures it. This bundle deliberately writes registry.xml — that is the deliverable, not an incidental measurement — and --retire, which this bundle invokes, writes the findings siblings and the citation index. The tension is stated so it is not a silent D30 breach.

One row's Pays may name several findings; four rows carry all of the set. Pays is the load-bearing field. StatusText may also contain a Closed with clause naming the same tokens (derivePayerMap's second loop) but must not be the only path.

--retire is this bundle's move, not a follow-on. After the four rows exist in live registry.xml, one bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --retire invocation stamps PaidBy, moves the four rows to registry-retired.xml (name equals an archive directory), moves the paid findings to findings-retired.xml (PaidBy names those archive events), and flips the matching RecordIndex Entry layer attributes. Validation then exits 0. The findings window opens by Delta_retired of the moved finding elements under the formula C-RETIREMENT-WINDOW shipped. The staged buffer is still not flushed — that remains the authority's act once the window covers it.

Registry ceiling never breached in any committed tree. Live occupancy after insert and before --retire is the pre-insert live row count plus the four historical rows, and that sum must be less than or equal to the persisted registry ceiling (dated occupancy is in Assumptions). --retire then returns live occupancy to the pre-insert count and persistSnapshot keeps the previous ceiling (min of that ceiling and post-move base plus the shipped registry headroom). The intermediate occupancy is a working-tree state between the insert and --retire in the same execution wave, never a commit validate:ci can see. Writing the rows directly into registry-retired.xml is refused: the maintainer ruled historical rows are written into registry.xml.

Constraints.Constraint: Ceremony tier T1 (module-change shape): the retirement validator and the record it governs. No graph module is written. Gates still run. Roadmap RM-GOVERNED-PATH. Binding live rulings: D28, D28.1, D30, D11. Staged D36 charters this name at position 6; do not mint a live chartered row for C-PAYMENT-RECORD (the staged charter row is the authority's flush). Paid live findings: the set named in Goals.

kind="historical", argued. Reusing kind="chartered" would make the derivation see the row with no code change, and is refused: these bundles were never chartered in advance in this registry, and a closed union that lies about its members is the same class of defect D28.1 named for a budget whose cheapest remedy is a config edit — the enforcement becomes a formality. kind="sweep-remainder" is the leftover-name table, Pays empty, and the filter already excludes it; stuffing payments there would also be a lie and would stay invisible. A fourth kind other than historical is not needed. The product change is the union plus the filter plus a validator error on any other kind value.

StatusText, required and true, not a derivation predicate. collectPaidBy / derivePayerMap do not require StatusText to match /delivered|superseded/i. Historical StatusText begins with **Delivered** because each named bundle is archived with spec and plan status="applied" (measured), then says the row is a historical payment record written by C-PAYMENT-RECORD because the archived spec never used the payer phrase and no registry row existed at close, then names the present-tree witness. It does not claim the range-hole or regenerate residuals. Number may be empty. Charter describes what that archived bundle delivered and that the row exists so the derivation can see the payment. status="live" on insert; --retire rewrites it to "retired".

Payment evidence, the load-bearing rule. Recording a payment that did not happen would retire live governance text on a false premise, which is D28.1's defect in a worse form: it converts eligibility — the enforcement itself — into a formality. Bulk attribution by plausibility is the failure mode this Constraint exists to refuse.
Sufficient, all of: (1) a present-tree witness — a symbol, a named test, or a file:line of the shipped behaviour that discharges the finding's defect; (2) the archived bundle that introduced that witness, with spec and plan status="applied"; (3) that bundle has no registry row in either sibling and its spec lacks the payer phrase, so the row is the only route; (4) the finding is still live, else the derivation already sees it.
Insufficient, each refused: a bundle name or charter topic that merely sounds related; the finding's own "discharged by" sentence without a tree check (a finding is never evidence of present state); Pays prose on a different row; sharing a file with a paid finding; a dated finding cited as HEAD; F90.1's range-hole and regenerate residuals, which remain unpaid NonGoals of C-CURSOR-TASK-RESOLVER and have no separate live token. F35.1 and F36 are not in this payment set: F35.1 is a weak TargetAssertion on a different bundle, and F36 was not re-verified for this spec.

Order, ceiling, and CI. Live occupancy after insert and before --retire is the pre-insert live row count plus the number of historical rows this bundle inserts, and that sum must be less than or equal to the persisted registry ceiling. The insert count is the size of the payment set in Goals. A commit that holds the rows without the move is ineligible: validation reports registry-eligible-still-live and finding-eligible-still-live until --retire runs. Do not raise the persisted ceiling.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-KIND-VISIBLE:
A fixture registry row with kind="historical", name equal to an archive directory, Pays naming a live finding token, and StatusText that does not match /delivered|superseded/i, appears in the payer map and makes that finding eligible. The same fixture with kind="sweep-remainder" and the same Pays does not. A kind="chartered" row still pays as today. A Row whose kind is not in the closed union (chartered | sweep-remainder | historical) makes the non-mutating validate run exit non-zero. Failure: historical rows are inert; sweep-remainder pays; an unknown kind is silently dropped.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-PAYMENT-SET:
After this bundle's --retire, the four names C-CURSOR-TASK-RESOLVER, C-SUBSTANCE-OVER-NAME, C-DECLARED-WRITES, and C-GRAMMAR-SEAM exist as kind="historical" rows in registry-retired.xml and not in live registry.xml; live findings.xml has no Finding whose token is F90, F90.1, F35, F27, F27.1, F27.2, or F38; those tokens exist as status="retired" with a PaidBy child naming the corresponding archive event; bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts exits 0. A production test that reads the real record carries an explicit generous timeout (staged F185). Failure: a named finding is still live; a named row is still live; PaidBy was hand-written rather than stamped by --retire; validate exits non-zero.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CEILING-ORDER:
An isolated fixture whose live registry snapshot matches the production ceiling formula, with the pre-insert live row count plus four historical archive- named rows still less than or equal to the persisted ceiling, persists that ceiling across --retire, returns live occupancy to the pre-insert count, and places the four rows in the retired sibling. The fixture observes the live file after insert and before --retire so the order is not vacuous: a write that planted the rows directly in the retired sibling fails this probe. Failure: the persisted ceiling rises; live occupancy after --retire still includes an archive-named row; the intermediate occupancy was never in live registry.xml.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-WINDOW-FUEL:
An isolated fixture --retire that moves the payment-set's finding elements opens a findings window of H + Delta_retired under the shipped C-RETIREMENT-WINDOW formula (ceiling stays the previously persisted value when Base_live + H meets or exceeds it; base drops by the moved lines; headroom = ceiling - base). Production wrap of the payment set and of the staged buffer is in Assumptions, not pinned here. Failure: the move does not open window; the ceiling drops with the content the way the pre-window clamp did.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
